result.summary: The pedestrian environment is a residential street with sidewalks but lacks any formal crossing infrastructure such as marked crosswalks or traffic control signs. Large street trees and parked vehicles create potential sightline obstructions at the unmarked intersection area.

hazards.name: Unmarked Crossing
hazards.description: There are no painted crosswalks at the intersection, forcing pedestrians to cross without a designated space.
hazards.location_in_image: Center foreground where the streets meet.

hazards.name: Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: Large trees and parked vehicles along the curb may hide pedestrians from oncoming traffic.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Paint continental-style crosswalks to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility for both pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Traffic Control Signage
interventions.description: Install stop signs or pedestrian crossing warning signs to manage vehicle speeds and awareness.

result.summary: The environment features a marked zebra crosswalk and wide, well-maintained sidewalks with modern curb ramps. However, the lack of visible traffic control devices and sightline obstructions from parked cars near the crossing increase potential risk for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: Parked vehicles on both sides of the street are positioned very close to the crosswalk, obscuring the view between drivers and pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the curbs on both sides of the street approaching the crosswalk

hazards.name: Lack of Traffic Control
hazards.description: There are no visible stop signs, signals, or pedestrian warning signs at this crossing to manage vehicle right-of-way.

hazards.name: Degraded Road Surface
hazards.description: The asphalt shows significant cracking and patching, which can create tripping hazards or uneven surfaces for pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Roadway surface within and around the crosswalk

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces immediately adjacent to the crosswalk to improve visibility for both pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions (bulb-outs) to shorten the crossing distance and prevent illegal parking near the intersection.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Crossing Signage
interventions.description: Install high-visibility pedestrian crossing signs or an in-street 'Yield to Pedestrians' sign to alert drivers.

result.summary: The street features a wide, well-maintained sidewalk on the left adjacent to a modern residential building, but lacks a sidewalk on the right side. There are no marked crosswalks, lane markings, or pedestrian signals visible, creating a significant gap in the pedestrian network.

hazards.name: Missing Sidewalk
hazards.description: The right side of the street lacks a sidewalk, forcing pedestrians to walk in the roadway if they need to access that side.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the street along the brick wall.

hazards.name: Lack of Marked Crossings
hazards.description: There are no designated or marked places for pedestrians to cross the street safely.

interventions.title: Install Sidewalk
interventions.description: Construct a sidewalk on the right side of the street to provide a continuous and safe pedestrian path on both sides.

interventions.title: Marked Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install high-visibility crosswalks to provide designated crossing points for pedestrians.

interventions.title: Lane Markings
interventions.description: Add center lines and edge lines to better define the travel way and organize vehicle movements.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is characterized by an industrial setting with narrow, obstructed sidewalks and a complete lack of formal crossing infrastructure. The presence of pallets on the walkway and the absence of lane markings or signage create a hazardous space for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstruction
hazards.description: Wooden pallets are stacked on the sidewalk, forcing pedestrians into the roadway.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side, adjacent to the brick building

hazards.name: Lack of Marked Crossing
hazards.description: No designated crossing area exists for pedestrians to traverse the wide roadway.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction
hazards.description: The building corner and stacked pallets limit visibility between drivers and pedestrians at the corner.

interventions.title: Clear Sidewalk Obstructions
interventions.description: Enforce regulations to keep the sidewalk clear of commercial goods and pallets to ensure a continuous walking path.

interventions.title: Install Marked Crosswalks and Curb Ramps
interventions.description: Provide high-visibility crosswalks and ADA-compliant curb ramps to facilitate safe and accessible crossing.

interventions.title: Add Street Lighting
interventions.description: Install pedestrian-scale lighting to improve visibility and safety during low-light conditions.
